subject: Next steps: Acme Robotics private deployment — allowlist & connectivity decisions
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@acmerobotics.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + action items (Private deployment choices / allowlist)

Hi John / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and clear asks so we can keep the Private deployment evaluation moving: 

Call summary (high level):
- Goal: Host sensitive inference workloads for Acme Robotics in a private network with no public internet egress for model requests.
- Options on the table: Hosted API (not acceptable due to data residency), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), Redwood Private via AWS PrivateLink or VPC Peering (customer VPC).

Immediate asks / next steps (what we need from you):
1) Confirm connectivity preference: PrivateLink (AWS NLB + interface ENIs) vs VPC peering. If you have an internal preference, tell us why (e.g., central security posture, cross-account constraints).
2) Fill the attached allowlist template (acme-mrp-allowlist-template.csv) with the egress IP ranges you allow (or the CIDR ranges we should peer to). If you prefer, provide your network team's contact and we can run a short triage call.
3) Tell us whether you require dedicated reserved capacity (Guarnteed throughput) vs. whether burstable/dedicated is OK. If you have throughput estimates (reqs per second, tokens/min), paste them here.
4) Confirm vault/KMS requirements (bring-your-own-key?) and whether you need HSM for keys.

Technical notes for your network team:
- PrivateLink: requires us to create a service in our account and you to accept the interface endpoint in your VPC; no route table changes on your side but you will get interface ENIs (recommended if cross-account peering is restricted).
- VPC Peering: simpler routing for same-region, cheaper, but requires route updates and does not support transitive routing.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-vpc-one-pager.pdf (summary of deployment modes), acme-mrp-allowlist-template.csv (fillable).

Proposed next touch: Thu Sep 23, 09:00–09:30 PT — 30m network triage with your cloud / netops. Confirm if that works and which internal attendees (network/security) will join.

Thanks — I’ll hand off any deep network questions to Ben (cc) and Marissa for SRE/infra questions.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-vpc-one-pager.pdf (1 page), acme-mrp-allowlist-template.csv (CSV template)

From: John Park <john.park@acmerobotics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 17:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + action items (Private deployment choices / allowlist)

Hannah —

Appreciate the recap. Quick answers from our side to keep momentum: 

1) Connectivity preference: We lean toward PrivateLink because our security team prefers interface endpoints and we avoid managing route tables. However, we need confirmation on cost implications and whether PrivateLink will add latency for bursty workloads.

2) Attached is our initial network diagram (internal_netdiag_v2.pdf) and our current allowlist ranges — see below. I’m pasting the ranges here so you can start testing before we share the CSV formally:
- 10.12.0.0/20 (app subnet)
- 10.20.16.0/20 (edge services)

We also have a small set of NAT-ed egress IPs for outbound services; we can share those if you need concrete public IPs for an allowlist.

3) Throughput: For phase 1 we expect ~25 RPS with average 400 tokens/request; peak 100 RPS during batch jobs. If Dedicated capacity gives predictable latency at that scale, we’d like numbers on cost vs hosted.

4) KMS: We require BYOK with AWS KMS key in our account (cross-account key grants ok). We do not need HSM today.

We’ll have our network lead (Samantha) on the triage call — Thu 23 Sep 09:00 PT works.

Thanks,
John Park
Head of Platform — Acme Robotics
john.park@acmerobotics.com | +1 (206) 555-4820

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@acmerobotics.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acmerobotics.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + action items (Private deployment choices / allowlist)

John / Samantha —

Thanks for the details and ranges. I’ll keep this short and tactical:

PrivateLink vs VPC peering — quick pros/cons for your network/security teams:
- PrivateLink:
  * Pros: No route table changes, fine-grained service acceptance, works across accounts and org boundaries, recommended when security policy blocks peering.
  * Cons: Interface ENIs per subnet (visibility), small per-endpoint data processing charges at AWS; additional setup but fewer cross-account firewall rules.
- VPC Peering:
  * Pros: Simpler data path for same-region traffic, potentially lower egress cost depending on topology.
  * Cons: Requires route propagation, not transitive, requires peering acceptance and possibly AWS support if you have overlapping CIDRs.

Recommendation for Acme (based on what John described):
- PrivateLink is the conservative path given your security posture and BYOK requirement for KMS — it keeps control with your VPC and reduces blast radius.
- If latency at peak 100 RPS is a concern, Dedicated capacity gives consistent tail latency — we can run a short perf test in our hosted environment vs a dedicated worker to quantify.

Concrete asks from Redwood to your NetOps ahead of the triage call: 
1) Share the public IPs/NAT egress set (if you want us to allow outbound to your NAT). If you prefer PrivateLink, we need the subnets where you will create the interface endpoints (one per AZ).
2) Confirm VPC IDs, AZ footprint, and whether you have Egress-only firewalls that will affect interface connectivity.
3) Provide the IAM principal/role we can use for cross-account KMS grants (ARN).

I’ve attached the deployment one-pager and a short planning checklist. During the Thu call we’ll scope a short mutual-action plan (3–4 week pilot suggested).

Planned triage agenda (15–20m):
- Quick architecture consensus (PrivateLink vs Peering)
- IP/ENI/Route requirements alignment
- BYOK/KMS cross-account mapping
- Next steps / pilot timeline

If you want, I can run an internal perf sim and share numbers before the call.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0110
